contexts.text: The things he produces in the fifth state are animate, and are called the fishes of the sea, and the birds of the heavens.
Fishes = scientifics. Illustrated. AC 3424.
Fishers from En-gedi to En-eglaim with the spreading out of nets () = those who teach the natural man about the truths of faith.
Fishes () = scientifics, here, made alive by means of faith from the Lord.
Under Beast, see this reference.
To their left there appear great fishes, monstrous whales, which swallow and then vomit forth a man.

To all the fishes of the sea () = scientifics. Fishes, in the Word, = the scientifics which originate from sensuous things; for there are scientifics of three kinds, - intellectual, rational, and sensuous... The scientifics which are from sensuous things come to the sensation or perception of man while he lives in the body, for he thinks from them.
The fishes of the sea () = lower rational things, or man's thought from sensuous scientifics.
To make a man as the fishes of the sea () = altogether sensuous.
The fishers () = those who trust only in sensuous things.
Much fish () = an abundance of applicable scientifics. AC 9050:10. AE 179:7.
Fishers () = those who teach from sensuous truths; hunters, those who teach from scientific truths...
The honeycomb and the broiled fish which the Lord ate after His resurrection, = the external sense of the Word; the fish, as to its truth.
Peter's taking a fish out of the sea, and finding in its mouth a piece of money, which he gave, represented that the lowest Natural as a thing that serves would do this; for fishes = this Natural.
Fishes = the scientifics which are under a general principle.
A whale, which is the largest fish of the sea, ... = what is scientific in genera], because a fish = what is scientific in particular.
The fish which is in the river shall die () = that what is scientific of truth will be extinguished. A fish = what is scientific...
A fish = the truth of the Natural.
Their fish shall be putrid () = the Scientific which is of the natural man.
They eat the flesh of fishes only.
To fish them () = to instruct in the external things of the Church.
Like fish out of the water. CL 10:6.
They are compared to fishes (in the parable, ), because by fishes, in the Word, are signified natural and external men, both good and evil.
A fish = knowledge. (See Dagon, and at DFaith 52.)
Imperfect animals, are fishes...
An image of the infinite... in the prolification... of fishes... TCR 32:3.

These are the things which are meant in the Word by the fishes of the sea, which are sensuous affections, that is, the lowest affections of the natural man; for, in the Spiritual World, the affections of such appear at a distance as fishes, and as it were in the sea.

The fishes, or creatures of the sea, mentioned in these passages, = the affections and derivative thoughts of those men who are in natural truths, and who thus partake more of the Natural than of the Spiritual.

The fishes of the rivers of Egypt () = those who are in doctrinal things, and, from them, are in faith separated, which faith is only knowledge; and it was on account of this separation, that... their waters were turned into blood, and the fishes died in consequence.
Fishes, here, () = those who are in general truths, and in faith separated from charity. Hut fishes = those who are in general truths, and in faith conjoined with charity in ,  and .

He who knows that such people and things are signified by fishes can see why the Lord chose fishermen for His disciples, and said... I will make you fishers of men. Also why the disciples, by the Lord's blessing, caught a vast multitude of fishes... why the Lord (caused the tribute to be paid from the fish); and why, after His resurrection, He gave the disciples fish and bread to eat (), and commanded them to... preach the gospel to every creature; for the nations they converted were in general truths only, and in natural truth more than in spiritual.

I was once asked, How, from being a philosopher, I became a theologian; and I replied, In the same way that fishermen were made disciples and apostles by the Lord: and that also from early youth I had been a spiritual fisherman. On this my questioner asked, What is a spiritual fisherman? I replied, A fisherman, in the Word... = a man who investigates and teaches natural truths, and afterwards spiritual truths in a rational manner. Illustrated. ISB 20:3.

If the fishes of the sea were to multiply... they would fill the ocean, so that it would consist of nothing but fishes... to prevent this, it has been provided by God that one fish should be food for another.
If he closes the lowest natural degree... he becomes as to... the understanding of truth like a fish.
(Like) a fish against the ocean.
I compared them to fishes under the ice...
The fishes which then died = the truths in the natural man.
I said, Why did the Lord choose fishermen... and not priests... Discuss this...

When this Spirit was in the Lower Earth, there suddenly appeared a table with great fishes... one of which swallowed him... signifying the natural things which he loves in preference to spiritual things.
He whirled round as it were a roll in the form of a fish... (This) signified his natural things.
They then let down hooks, as it were, to draw them to themselves, like fishers.
Its body was like a scaly fish... The scaly fish = sensuous scientifics, whereby they are led into magical things.

What is meant by trailing a net, and hauling out fishes... When this devil was thinking... that he attracted the simple good, who were so because they were natural, he seemed to have a net, and to plunge it down and bring it up, and thus to draw the upright to him.

Their fish shall be putrid = that the scientifics of the natural man will be devoid of all spiritual life; which takes place when they are applied to confirm falsities in opposition to the truths of the Church.
The fish = true scientifics.
The fishes (with which the Lord fed the multitude) = goods and truths in the Natural.

The inhabitants of the lowest Heaven... appear as in a sea... At this day there is a vast number there, because so many at this day are sensuous... For this reason seas are so frequently mentioned in the Word, and also the fishes therein; for seas = the general principles of truth... and fishes, sensuous scientifics, which are the lowest things of the natural man, and therefore they = those who are such, that is, who are in these scientifics. Illustrated.
The fishes of the sea () = those who are in the ultimates of truth, in whom there is no life from a spiritual origin.
The birds of the heavens, and the fishes of the sea (; ; ) = affections of truth and thoughts both spiritual and natural (which are) about to perish.
The reason of this signification of the sea and of fishes, is founded on the appearance in the Spiritual World. Explained.

The reason why they who are in... natural affection and thought are signified by fishes, is also founded on the appearance in the Spiritual World; for there appear there... fishes... in the seas; and it is the affections and thoughts of those who are there which so appear... (Thus) seas = general principles of truth; and whales and fishes, the affections and thoughts of those who are in the general principles of truth.
They think merely naturally and sensuously... The good among them are like... flying fishes.
The fish of his rivers = what is sensuous scientific.
The fishes of the sea = natural things in general, and, specifically, the scientifics therein.
That the Church is to be established from those who are in natural good... is meant by I will send fishers who shall fish them ().
Much fish = an abundance of Knowledges and scientifics which will attain spiritual life with them.
The loaves (with which the Lord fed the multitude) = the goods; and the fishes, the truths, of the natural man.

The reason the creatures of the sea, or fishes, = scientifics, is that the sea = the natural man; consequently, the fishes in the sea = the scientifics themselves which are in the natural man... Spirits who are not in spiritual truths, but only in natural ones, which are scientifics, appear in seas, and, when looked at by those who are above, as fishes; it is their thoughts, which proceed from the scientifics with them, which so appear. For... the ideas of thought of those who are natural and think from scientifics only, are turned into the forms of fishes. Hence there appear in (those) seas many kinds of fish.
It is from this that fishes, in the Word, = scientifics. Illustrated.
The fish dying (in the Nile) = that scientific truths perished through falsities; for scientifics live through truths, but perish through falsities...
Their appetite for natural things is signified by their lusting for the fish of Egypt...

That there shall be true and living scientifics of every kind, is signified by, the fish being according to their kind, as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many (). They who are being reformed, and who thus become intelligent, are meant by the fishers from En-gedi even to En-eglaim.
Beast = the Voluntary; bird = the Intellectual; and fish = the Scientific. Illustrated.

As fishes = the scientifics and Knowledges of the natural man, which are of service to the spiritual man as a means of being wise, fishers, in the Word, = those who are only in Knowledges, and who acquire Knowledges for themselves; also, who teach others, and reform them by means of Knowledges. Their works are meant by the letting out and spreading out of nets. Illustrated.
To make men as the fishes of the sea () = to make man so natural that his scientifics are devoid of spiritual truth...
The fishes (of the great draught, ) = the Knowledges of truth and good by means of which there is reformation; and also the multitude of men who are being reformed.

Like things are signified by the catching of fishes by the disciples after the Lord's resurrection. The reason the Lord manifested Himself while they were fishing, was that to fish = to teach the Knowledges of truth and good, and thus to reform... By the little fish upon the hearth was signified the Knowledge of truth from good; by the little fish, the Knowledge of truth; and by the hearth, or fire, good. At that time there were no spiritual men, because the Church was completely vastated, but all were natural, and the reformation of these latter was represented by that fishing, and also by the fish upon the hearth.

The separation of the good from the evil is likened to a net bringing together fishes of every kind (), because fishes = natural men as to scientifics and Knowledges; and these are separated from each other at the Last Judgment; for there are good natural men and evil natural men; and the separation of these appears in the Spiritual World like a net let out into the sea and drawing fishes together into it, and bringing them to shore.
The broiled fish = the Natural as to truth from good... A broiled fish = what is scientific derived from natural good.
With hooks of fishing () = through the fallacies of the senses.
By fishing-piscationem in the Word, is signified the instruction and conversion of men who are in external or natural good, in which good there were many at that time among the gentiles.
The broiled fish = the truth of good of the natural and sensuous man.
Fish = the things which are in the natural man, which are called Knowledges from the Word, and also natural knowledges by means of which spiritual things are confirmed.
By the fishes of the sea are signified the scientifics of the natural sensuous man.
Fishes = scientifics. AE 1100:4.

The fishers shall lament... () = that those who teach will labour in vain to reform the natural man by means of truths from the Word: fishers, and they who spread the net = those who teach natural men from the Word, specifically, from the sense of the letter; fish = the Knowledges thence derived.
I will make the fish of thy rivers stick to thy scales () = false scientifics of the lowest kind which are from the fallacies of the senses.

The reason these three apostles were fishermen, and that it was said to them... I will make you fishers of men, was that to fish = to instruct natural men; for at that time there were natural men both within the Church and without it, who, as they received the Lord and truths from Him, became spiritual men.
A fish = the natural man.

By the living soul in the sea are meant fishes of various kinds, by which are signified the scientifics of the natural man; and also Knowledges of truth from the Word with natural men; for with such men Knowledges of truth from the Word are held just as are the scientifics of the world.
The fishes killed = the destruction of the true scientifics and of the Knowledges of the natural man.
Fishes of the sea = Knowledges and scientifics.
To consume the birds of the heavens and the fishes of the sea () = to destroy the perceptions and the Knowledges of truth.
